segs.p: Caṇḍasutta
segs.e: Fury

segs.p: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
segs.e: At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Fury the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some people are regarded as furious,

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti?
segs.e: while others are regarded as gentle?”

segs.p: “Idha, gāmaṇi, ekaccassa rāgo appahīno hoti.
segs.e: “Take someone who hasn’t given up greed.

segs.p: Rāgassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.

segs.p: So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as furious.

segs.p: Doso appahīno hoti.
segs.e: They haven’t given up hate.

segs.p: Dosassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.

segs.p: So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as furious.

segs.p: Moho appahīno hoti.
segs.e: They haven’t given up delusion.

segs.p: Mohassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they get annoyed by others, and they show it.

segs.p: So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as furious.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why some people are regarded as furious.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekaccassa rāgo pahīno hoti.
segs.e: But take someone who has given up greed.

segs.p: Rāgassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.

segs.p: So soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as gentle.

segs.p: Doso pahīno hoti.
segs.e: They’ve given up hate.

segs.p: Dosassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.

segs.p: So soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as gentle.

segs.p: Moho pahīno hoti.
segs.e: They’ve given up delusion.

segs.p: Mohassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṁ na pātukaroti.
segs.e: So they don’t get annoyed by others, and don’t show it.

segs.p: So soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: They’re regarded as gentle.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why some people are regarded as gentle.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Fury the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the Buddha has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Tālapuṭasutta
segs.e: With Tālapuṭa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Tālapuṭa the dancing chief came up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, pubbakānaṁ ācariyapācariyānaṁ naṭānaṁ bhāsamānānaṁ:
segs.e: “Sir, I have heard that the dancers of the past who were tutors of tutors said:

segs.p: ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṁ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Suppose a dancer entertains and amuses people on a stage or at a festival with mixed truth and lies. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of laughing gods.’

segs.p: Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?
segs.e: What does the Buddha say about this?”

segs.p: “Alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ. Mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī”ti.
segs.e: “Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me that.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time …

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, pubbakānaṁ ācariyapācariyānaṁ naṭānaṁ bhāsamānānaṁ:
‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṁ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti.
Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?
“Alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ. Mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī”ti.
Tatiyampi kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time Tālapuṭa said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, pubbakānaṁ ācariyapācariyānaṁ naṭānaṁ bhāsamānānaṁ:
segs.e: “Sir, I have heard that the dancers of the past who were tutors of tutors said:

segs.p: ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṁ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Suppose a dancer entertains and amuses people on a stage or at a festival with mixed truth and lies. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of laughing gods.’

segs.p: Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?
segs.e: What does the Buddha say about this?”

segs.p: “Addhā kho tyāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, na labhāmi:
segs.e: “Clearly, chief, I’m not getting through to you when I say:

segs.p: ‘alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ,
segs.e: ‘Enough, chief, let it be.

segs.p: mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī’ti.
segs.e: Don’t ask me that.’

segs.p: Api ca tyāhaṁ byākarissāmi.
segs.e: Nevertheless, I will answer you.

segs.p: Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi, sattā avītarāgā rāgabandhanabaddhā.
segs.e: When sentient beings are still not free of greed, and are still bound by greed,

segs.p: Tesaṁ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā rajanīyā te upasaṁharati bhiyyoso mattāya.
segs.e: a dancer in a stage or festival presents them with even more arousing things.

segs.p: Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi, sattā avītadosā dosabandhanabaddhā.
segs.e: When sentient beings are still not free of hate, and are still bound by hate,

segs.p: Tesaṁ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā dosanīyā te upasaṁharati bhiyyoso mattāya.
segs.e: a dancer in a stage or festival presents them with even more hateful things.

segs.p: Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi, sattā avītamohā mohabandhanabaddhā.
segs.e: When sentient beings are still not free of delusion, and are still bound by delusion,

segs.p: Tesaṁ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā mohanīyā te upasaṁharati bhiyyoso mattāya.
segs.e: a dancer in a stage or festival presents them with even more delusory things.

segs.p: So attanā matto pamatto pare madetvā pamādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāso nāma nirayo tattha upapajjati.
segs.e: And so, being heedless and negligent themselves, they’ve encouraged others to be heedless and negligent. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the hell called ‘Laughter’.

segs.p: Sace kho panassa evaṁdiṭṭhi hoti:
segs.e: But if you have such a view:

segs.p: ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṁ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti, sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: ‘Suppose a dancer entertains and amuses people on a stage or at a festival with mixed truth and lies. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of laughing gods.’ This is your wrong view.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhikassa kho panāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, purisapuggalassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: An individual with wrong view is reborn in one of two places, I say:

segs.p: nirayaṁ vā tiracchānayoniṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: hell or the animal realm.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi parodi assūni pavattesi.
segs.e: When he said this, Tālapuṭa cried and burst out in tears.

segs.p: “Etaṁ kho tyāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, nālatthaṁ:
segs.e: “This is what I didn’t get through to you when I said:

segs.p: ‘alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ; mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me that.’”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhante, etaṁ rodāmi yaṁ maṁ bhagavā evamāha;
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not crying because of what the Buddha said.

segs.p: api cāhaṁ, bhante, pubbakehi ācariyapācariyehi naṭehi dīgharattaṁ nikato vañcito paluddho:
segs.e: But sir, for a long time I’ve been cheated, tricked, and deceived by the dancers of the past who were tutors of tutors, who said:

segs.p: ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṁ hāseti rameti so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā pahāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Suppose a dancer entertains and amuses people on a stage or at a festival with mixed truth and lies. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of laughing gods.’

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the Buddha has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Labheyyāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyaṁ upasampadan”ti.
segs.e: Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?”

segs.p: Alattha kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And Tālapuṭa the dancing chief received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā tālapuṭo …pe…
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, Venerable Tālapuṭa

segs.p: arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.

segs.e: A Warrior

“Alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ; mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī”ti.
Dutiyampi kho …pe…
tatiyampi kho assāroho gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
“sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, pubbakānaṁ ācariyapācariyānaṁ assārohānaṁ bhāsamānānaṁ:
‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā parajitānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti.
Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?
“Addhā kho tyāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, na labhāmi:
‘alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ; mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī’ti.
Api ca kho tyāhaṁ byākarissāmi.
Yo so, gāmaṇi, assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati tassa taṁ cittaṁ pubbe gahitaṁ dukkaṭaṁ duppaṇihitaṁ:
‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā ahesuṁ iti vā’ti.
Tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā parajito nāma nirayo tattha upapajjati.
Sace kho panassa evaṁ diṭṭhi hoti:

‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā parajitānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’ti, sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi.
Micchādiṭṭhikassa kho panāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, purisapuggalassa dvinnaṁ gatīnaṁ aññataraṁ gatiṁ vadāmi—
nirayaṁ vā tiracchānayoniṁ vā”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, assāroho gāmaṇi parodi, assūni pavattesi.
“Etaṁ kho tyāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, nālatthaṁ:
‘alaṁ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṁ; mā maṁ etaṁ pucchī’”ti.
“Nāhaṁ, bhante, etaṁ rodāmi yaṁ maṁ bhagavā evamāha.
Api cāhaṁ, bhante, pubbakehi ācariyapācariyehi assārohehi dīgharattaṁ nikato vañcito paluddho:
‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā parajitānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī’”ti.
“Abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Pañcamaṁ.

segs.p: Asibandhakaputtasutta
segs.e: With Asibandhaka’s Son

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṁ viharati pāvārikambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Asibandhaka’s son the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “brāhmaṇā, bhante, pacchā bhūmakā kāmaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā udakorohakā aggiparicārakā.
segs.e: “Sir, there are western brahmins garlanded with aquatic flowers who carry pitchers, immerse themselves in water, and serve the sacred flame.

segs.p: Te mataṁ kālaṅkataṁ uyyāpenti nāma saññāpenti nāma saggaṁ nāma okkāmenti.
segs.e: When someone has passed away, oh! they lift them up, send them well, and convey them to heaven.

segs.p: Bhagavā pana, bhante, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho pahoti tathā kātuṁ yathā sabbo loko kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyā”ti?
segs.e: But what about the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha: is he able to ensure that the whole world will be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm when their body breaks up, after death?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, gāmaṇi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsīti.
segs.e: “Well then, chief, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: idhassa puriso pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko.
segs.e: Take a person who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, and have wrong view.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ mahājanakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: A large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty, circumambulating them with cupped palms and saying:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjatū’ti.
segs.e: ‘When this person’s body breaks up, after death, may they be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm!’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would that person be reborn in heaven because of their supplications?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, puriso mahatiṁ puthusilaṁ gambhīre udakarahade pakkhipeyya.
segs.e: “Chief, suppose a person were to throw a broad rock into a deep lake.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: And a large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty, circumambulating it with cupped palms, and saying:

segs.p: ‘ummujja, bho puthusile, uplava, bho puthusile, thalamuplava, bho puthusile’ti.
segs.e: ‘Rise, good rock! Float, good rock! Float to shore, good rock!’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: api nu sā puthusilā mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā ummujjeyya vā uplaveyya vā thalaṁ vā uplaveyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would that broad rock rise up or float because of their supplications?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko.
segs.e: “In the same way, take a person who kills living creatures, steals, and commits sexual misconduct. They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re covetous, malicious, and have wrong view.

segs.p: Kiñcāpi taṁ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: Even though a large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty …

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjatū’ti, atha kho so puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: idhassa puriso pāṇātipātā paṭivirato adinnādānā paṭivirato kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato musāvādā paṭivirato pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato samphappalāpā paṭivirato anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto sammādiṭṭhiko.
segs.e: Take a person who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: And a large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty, circumambulating them with cupped palms and saying:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjatū’ti.
segs.e: ‘When this person’s body breaks up, after death, may they be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell!’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would that person be reborn in hell because of their supplications?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, puriso sappikumbhaṁ vā telakumbhaṁ vā gambhīre udakarahade ogāhetvā bhindeyya. Tatra yāssa sakkharā vā kaṭhalā vā sā adhogāmī assa; yañca khvassa tatra sappi vā telaṁ vā taṁ uddhaṁ gāmi assa.
segs.e: “Chief, suppose a person were to sink a pot of ghee or oil into a deep lake and break it open. Its shards and chips would sink down, while the ghee or oil in it would rise up.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: And a large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty, circumambulating it with cupped palms and saying:

segs.p: ‘osīda, bho sappitela, saṁsīda, bho sappitela, adho gaccha, bho sappitelā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sink, good ghee or oil! Descend, good ghee or oil! Go down, good ghee or oil!’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: api nu taṁ sappitelaṁ mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā osīdeyya vā saṁsīdeyya vā adho vā gaccheyyā”ti?
segs.e: Would that ghee or oil sink and descend because of their supplications?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso pāṇātipātā paṭivirato, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato, samphappalāpā paṭivirato, anabhijjhālu, abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhiko,
segs.e: “In the same way, take a person who doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct. They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical. And they’re contented, kind-hearted, with right view.

segs.p: kiñcāpi taṁ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya:
segs.e: Even though a large crowd were to come together to offer up supplication and entreaty …

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjatū’ti, atha kho so puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyā”ti.
segs.e: when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Asibandhaka’s son the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! …

segs.p: ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.

segs.p: Khettūpamasutta
segs.e: The Simile of the Field

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṁ viharati pāvārikambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Asibandhaka’s son the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “nanu, bhante, bhagavā sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, doesn’t the Buddha live full of sympathy for all living beings?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharatī”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, chief.”

segs.p: “Atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā ekaccānaṁ sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, ekaccānaṁ no tathā sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ desetī”ti?
segs.e: “So why then, sir, do you teach some people thoroughly and others less thoroughly?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, gāmaṇi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: “Well then, chief, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi, idhassu kassakassa gahapatino tīṇi khettāni—ekaṁ khettaṁ aggaṁ, ekaṁ khettaṁ majjhimaṁ, ekaṁ khettaṁ hīnaṁ jaṅgalaṁ ūsaraṁ pāpabhūmi.
segs.e: What do you think? Suppose a farmer has three fields: one is good, one is average, and one is poor—bad ground of sand and salt.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi, asu kassako gahapati bījāni patiṭṭhāpetukāmo kattha paṭhamaṁ patiṭṭhāpeyya, yaṁ vā aduṁ khettaṁ aggaṁ, yaṁ vā aduṁ khettaṁ majjhimaṁ, yaṁ vā aduṁ khettaṁ hīnaṁ jaṅgalaṁ ūsaraṁ pāpabhūmī”ti?
segs.e: What do you think? When that farmer wants to plant seeds, where would he plant them first: the good field, the average one, or the poor one?”

segs.p: “Asu, bhante, kassako gahapati bījāni patiṭṭhāpetukāmo yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ aggaṁ tattha patiṭṭhāpeyya. Tattha patiṭṭhāpetvā yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ majjhimaṁ tattha patiṭṭhāpeyya. Tattha patiṭṭhāpetvā yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ hīnaṁ jaṅgalaṁ ūsaraṁ pāpabhūmi tattha patiṭṭhāpeyyapi, nopi patiṭṭhāpeyya.
segs.e: “Sir, he’d plant them first in the good field, then the average, then he may or may not plant seed in the poor field.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Antamaso gobhattampi bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: Because at least it can be fodder for the cattle.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ aggaṁ; evameva mayhaṁ bhikkhubhikkhuniyo.
segs.e: “To me, the monks and nuns are like the good field.

segs.p: Tesāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ, sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṁdīpā maṁleṇā maṁtāṇā maṁsaraṇā viharanti.
segs.e: Because they live with me as their island, asylum, shelter, and refuge.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ majjhimaṁ; evameva mayhaṁ upāsakaupāsikāyo.
segs.e: To me, the laymen and laywomen are like the average field.

segs.p: Tesaṁ pāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ, sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I also teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṁdīpā maṁleṇā maṁtāṇā maṁsaraṇā viharanti.
segs.e: Because they live with me as their island, asylum, shelter, and refuge.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṁ aduṁ khettaṁ hīnaṁ jaṅgalaṁ ūsaraṁ pāpabhūmi; evameva mayhaṁ aññatitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakā.
segs.e: To me, the ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of other religions are like the poor field, the bad ground of sand and salt.

segs.p: Tesaṁ pāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I also teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Appeva nāma ekaṁ padampi ājāneyyuṁ taṁ nesaṁ assa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyāti.
segs.e: Hopefully they might understand even a single sentence, which would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, purisassa tayo udakamaṇikā—eko udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī, eko udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī, eko udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī.
segs.e: Suppose a person had three water jars: one that’s uncracked and nonporous; one that’s uncracked but porous; and one that’s cracked and porous.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi, asu puriso udakaṁ nikkhipitukāmo kattha paṭhamaṁ nikkhipeyya, yo vā so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī, yo vā so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī, yo vā so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī”ti?
segs.e: What do you think? When that person wants to store water, where would they store it first: in the jar that’s uncracked and nonporous, the one that’s uncracked but porous, or the one that’s cracked and porous?”

segs.p: “Asu, bhante, puriso udakaṁ nikkhipitukāmo, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī tattha nikkhipeyya, tattha nikkhipitvā, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī tattha nikkhipeyya, tattha nikkhipitvā, yo so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī tattha nikkhipeyyapi, nopi nikkhipeyya.
segs.e: “Sir, they’d store water first in the jar that’s uncracked and nonporous, then the one that’s uncracked but porous, then they may or may not store water in the one that’s cracked and porous.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Antamaso bhaṇḍadhovanampi bhavissatī”ti.
segs.e: Because at least it can be used for washing the dishes.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī; evameva mayhaṁ bhikkhubhikkhuniyo.
segs.e: “To me, the monks and nuns are like the water jar that’s uncracked and nonporous.

segs.p: Tesāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṁdīpā maṁleṇā maṁtāṇā maṁsaraṇā viharanti.
segs.e: Because they live with me as their island, asylum, shelter, and refuge.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī; evameva mayhaṁ upāsakaupāsikāyo.
segs.e: To me, the laymen and laywomen are like the water jar that’s uncracked but porous.

segs.p: Tesāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I also teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṁdīpā maṁleṇā maṁtāṇā maṁsaraṇā viharanti.
segs.e: Because they live with me as their island, asylum, shelter, and refuge.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī; evameva mayhaṁ aññatitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakā.
segs.e: To me, the ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of other religions are like the water jar that’s cracked and porous.

segs.p: Tesāhaṁ dhammaṁ desemi—ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāsemi.
segs.e: I also teach them the Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And I reveal a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Taṁ kissa hetu?
segs.e: Why is that?

segs.p: Appeva nāma ekaṁ padampi ājāneyyuṁ, taṁ nesaṁ assa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: Hopefully they might understand even a single sentence, which would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Asibandhaka’s son the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṁ viharati pāvārikambavane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhasāvako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho asibandhakaputtaṁ gāmaṇiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Asibandhaka’s son the chief, who was a disciple of the Jains, went up to the Buddha, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “kathaṁ nu kho, gāmaṇi, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṁ dhammaṁ desetī”ti?
segs.e: “Chief, how does the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan teach his disciples?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ kho, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: “Sir, this is how the Jain Ñātika teaches his disciples:

segs.p: ‘yo koci pāṇaṁ atipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci adinnaṁ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci musā bhaṇati sabbo, so āpāyiko nerayiko.
segs.e: ‘Everyone who kills a living creature, steals, commits sexual misconduct, or lies goes to a place of loss, to hell.

segs.p: Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulaṁ viharati, tena tena nīyatī’ti.
segs.e: You’re led on by what you frequently live by.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṁ dhammaṁ desetī”ti.
segs.e: This is how the Jain Ñātika teaches his disciples.”

segs.p: “‘Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati, tena tena nīyati’, evaṁ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṁ.
segs.e: “‘You’re led on by what you usually live by’: if this were true, then, according to what the Jain Ñātika says, no one would go to a place of loss, to hell.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: yo so puriso pāṇātipātī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṁ vā so pāṇamatipāteti, yaṁ vā so pāṇaṁ nātipātetī”ti?
segs.e: Take a person who kills living creatures. If we compare periods of time during the day and night, which is more frequent: the occasions when they’re killing or when they’re not killing?”

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, puriso pāṇātipātī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, appataro so samayo yaṁ so pāṇamatipāteti, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo yaṁ so pāṇaṁ nātipātetī”ti.
segs.e: “The occasions when they’re killing are less frequent, while the occasions when they’re not killing are more frequent.”

segs.p: “‘Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṁ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṁ.
segs.e: “‘You’re led on by what you usually live by’: if this were true, then, according to what the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan says, no one would go to a place of loss, to hell.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: yo so puriso adinnādāyī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṁ vā so adinnaṁ ādiyati, yaṁ vā so adinnaṁ nādiyatī”ti.
segs.e: Take a person who steals …

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, puriso adinnādāyī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya appataro so samayo, yaṁ so adinnaṁ ādiyati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṁ so adinnaṁ nādiyatī”ti.
“‘Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṁ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṁ.
Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso kāmesumicchācārī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṁ vā so kāmesu micchā carati, yaṁ vā so kāmesu micchā na caratī”ti?
segs.e: Take a person who commits sexual misconduct …

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, puriso kāmesumicchācārī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, appataro so samayo yaṁ so kāmesu micchā carati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṁ so kāmesu micchā na caratī”ti.
“‘Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṁ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṁ.
Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso musāvādī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṁ vā so musā bhaṇati, yaṁ vā so musā na bhaṇatī”ti?
segs.e: Take a person who lies. If we compare periods of time during the day and night, which is more frequent: the occasions when they’re lying or when they’re not lying?”

segs.p: “Yo so, bhante, puriso musāvādī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṁ upādāya, appataro so samayo, yaṁ so musā bhaṇati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṁ so musā na bhaṇatī”ti.
segs.e: “The occasions when they’re lying are less frequent, while the occasions when they’re not lying are more frequent.”

segs.p: “‘Yaṁbahulaṁ yaṁbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṁ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṁ.
segs.e: “‘You’re led on by what you usually live by’: if this were true, then, according to what the Jain Ñātika says, no one would go to a place of loss, to hell.

segs.p: Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco satthā evaṁvādī hoti evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: Take some teacher who has this doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘yo koci pāṇamatipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci adinnaṁ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci musā bhaṇati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko’ti.
segs.e: ‘Everyone who kills a living creature, steals, commits sexual misconduct, or lies goes to a place of loss, to hell.’

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, gāmaṇi, satthari sāvako abhippasanno hoti.
segs.e: And there’s a disciple who is devoted to that teacher.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: They think:

segs.p: ‘mayhaṁ kho satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi—
segs.e: ‘My teacher has this doctrine and view:

segs.p: yo koci pāṇamatipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti.
segs.e: “Everyone who kills a living creature, steals, commits sexual misconduct, or lies goes to a place of loss, to hell.”

segs.p: Atthi kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito, ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayikoti diṭṭhiṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: But I’ve killed living creatures …

segs.p: Taṁ, gāmaṇi, vācaṁ appahāya taṁ cittaṁ appahāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
Mayhaṁ kho satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi—
yo koci adinnaṁ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti.
Atthi kho pana mayā adinnaṁ ādinnaṁ ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayikoti diṭṭhiṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: stolen …

segs.p: Taṁ, gāmaṇi, vācaṁ appahāya taṁ cittaṁ appahāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
Mayhaṁ kho satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi—
yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko’ti.
Atthi kho pana mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṁ.
segs.e: committed sexual misconduct …

segs.p: ‘Ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayiko’ti diṭṭhiṁ paṭilabhati.
Taṁ, gāmaṇi, vācaṁ appahāya taṁ cittaṁ appahāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
Mayhaṁ kho satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi—
yo koci musā bhaṇati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti.
Atthi kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṁ.
segs.e: or lied.’

segs.p: ‘Ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayiko’ti diṭṭhiṁ paṭilabhati.
segs.e: They get the view: ‘I too am going to a place of loss, to hell.’

segs.p: Taṁ, gāmaṇi, vācaṁ appahāya taṁ cittaṁ appahāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Unless they give up that speech and that thought, and let go of that view, they will be placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā.
segs.e: But consider when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.

segs.p: So anekapariyāyena pāṇātipātaṁ garahati vigarahati, ‘pāṇātipātā viramathā’ti cāha.
segs.e: In many ways he criticizes and denounces killing living creatures, saying: ‘Stop killing living creatures!’

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ garahati vigarahati, ‘adinnādānā viramathā’ti cāha.
segs.e: He criticizes and denounces stealing …

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāraṁ garahati, vigarahati ‘kāmesumicchācārā viramathā’ti cāha.
segs.e: sexual misconduct …

segs.p: Musāvādaṁ garahati vigarahati ‘musāvādā viramathā’ti cāha.
segs.e: lying, saying: ‘Stop lying!’

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, gāmaṇi, satthari sāvako abhippasanno hoti.
segs.e: And there’s a disciple who is devoted to that teacher.

segs.p: So iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Then they reflect:

segs.p: ‘bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena pāṇātipātaṁ garahati vigarahati, pāṇātipātā viramathāti cāha.
segs.e: ‘In many ways the Buddha criticizes and denounces killing living creatures, saying: “Stop killing living creatures!”

segs.p: Atthi kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito yāvatako vā tāvatako vā.
segs.e: But I have killed living creatures to a certain extent.

segs.p: Yo kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito yāvatako vā tāvatako vā, taṁ na suṭṭhu, taṁ na sādhu.
segs.e: That’s not right, it’s not good,

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṁ.
segs.e: and I feel remorseful because of it.

segs.p: Na metaṁ pāpaṁ kammaṁ akataṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: But I can’t undo what I have done.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva pāṇātipātaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up killing living creatures,

segs.p: Āyatiñca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: and in future they don’t kill living creatures.

segs.p: Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṁ hoti.
segs.e: That’s how to give up this bad deed

segs.p: Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.
segs.e: and get past it.

segs.p: ‘Bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena adinnādānaṁ garahati vigarahati, adinnādānā viramathāti cāha.
segs.e: ‘In many ways the Buddha criticizes and denounces stealing …’

segs.p: Atthi kho pana mayā adinnaṁ ādinnaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā.
Yaṁ kho pana mayā adinnaṁ ādinnaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā taṁ na suṭṭhu, taṁ na sādhu.
Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṁ, na metaṁ pāpaṁ kammaṁ akataṁ bhavissatī’ti.
So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva adinnādānaṁ pajahati.
Āyatiñca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti.
Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṁ hoti.
Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.
‘Bhagavā kho pana anekapariyāyena kāmesumicchācāraṁ garahati vigarahati, kāmesumicchācārā viramathāti cāha.
segs.e: ‘In many ways the Buddha criticizes and denounces sexual misconduct …’

segs.p: Atthi kho pana mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā.
Yaṁ kho pana mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā taṁ na suṭṭhu, taṁ na sādhu.
Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṁ, na metaṁ pāpaṁ kammaṁ akataṁ bhavissatī’ti.
So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva kāmesumicchācāraṁ pajahati, āyatiñca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti.
Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṁ hoti.
Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.
‘Bhagavā kho pana anekapariyāyena musāvādaṁ garahati vigarahati, musāvādā viramathāti cāha.
segs.e: ‘In many ways the Buddha criticizes and denounces lying, saying: “Stop lying!”

segs.p: Atthi kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā.
segs.e: But I have lied to a certain extent.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṁ yāvatakaṁ vā tāvatakaṁ vā taṁ na suṭṭhu, taṁ na sādhu. Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṁ, na metaṁ pāpaṁ kammaṁ akataṁ bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: That’s not right, it’s not good, and I feel remorseful because of it. But I can’t undo what I have done.’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva musāvādaṁ pajahati, āyatiñca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: Reflecting like this, they give up lying, and in future they refrain from lying.

segs.p: Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṁ hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how to give up this bad deed and get past it.

segs.p: So pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up killing living creatures.

segs.p: Adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up stealing.

segs.p: Kāmesumicchācāraṁ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up sexual misconduct.

segs.p: Musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up lying.

segs.p: Pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up backbiting.

segs.p: Pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up harsh speech.

segs.p: Samphappalāpaṁ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They give up talking nonsense.

segs.p: Abhijjhaṁ pahāya anabhijjhālu hoti.
segs.e: They give up covetousness.

segs.p: Byāpādappadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto hoti.
segs.e: They give up ill will and malevolence.

segs.p: Micchādiṭṭhiṁ pahāya sammādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: They give up wrong view and have right view.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako evaṁ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: That noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva catuddisā viññāpeyya;
segs.e: Suppose there was a powerful horn blower. They’d easily make themselves heard in the four quarters.

segs.p: evameva kho, gāmaṇi, evaṁ bhāvitāya mettāya cetovimuttiyā evaṁ bahulīkatāya yaṁ pamāṇakataṁ kammaṁ, na taṁ tatrāvasissati, na taṁ tatrāvatiṭṭhati.
segs.e: In the same way, when the heart’s release by love has been developed and cultivated like this, any limited deeds they’ve done don’t remain or persist there.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako evaṁ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato karuṇāsahagatena cetasā …pe…
segs.e: Then that noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …

segs.p: muditāsahagatena cetasā …pe….
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of rejoicing …

segs.p: Upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: They meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva catuddisā viññāpeyya;
segs.e: Suppose there was a powerful horn blower. They’d easily make themselves heard in the four quarters.

segs.p: evameva kho, gāmaṇi, evaṁ bhāvitāya upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā evaṁ bahulīkatāya yaṁ pamāṇakataṁ kammaṁ na taṁ tatrāvasissati, na taṁ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, when the heart’s release by equanimity has been developed and cultivated like this, any limited deeds they’ve done don’t remain or persist there.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Asibandhaka’s son the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 42.9
segs.e: Linked Discourses 42.9

segs.p: 1. Gāmaṇivagga
segs.e: 1. Chiefs

segs.p: Kulasutta
segs.e: Families

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena nāḷandā tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at Nāḷandā.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṁ viharati pāvārikambavane.
segs.e: There he stayed near Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s Mango Grove.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena nāḷandā dubbhikkhā hoti dvīhitikā setaṭṭhikā salākāvuttā.
segs.e: Now at that time Nāḷandā was undergoing famine and scarcity, with crops blighted and turned to straw.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nāḷandāyaṁ paṭivasati mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṁ.
segs.e: At that time the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan was residing at Nāḷandā together with a large assembly of Jain ascetics.

segs.p: Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhasāvako yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho asibandhakaputtaṁ gāmaṇiṁ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Asibandhaka’s son the chief, who was a disciple of the Jains, went up to the Jain Ñātika, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Jain Ñātika said to him:

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, gāmaṇi, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṁ āropehi.
segs.e: “Come, chief, refute the ascetic Gotama’s doctrine.

segs.p: Evaṁ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati:
segs.e: Then you will get a good reputation:

segs.p: ‘asibandhakaputtena gāmaṇinā samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁmahiddhikassa evaṁmahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Asibandhaka’s son the chief refuted the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama, so mighty and powerful!’”

segs.p: “Kathaṁ panāhaṁ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṁmahiddhikassa evaṁmahānubhāvassa vādaṁ āropessāmī”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, how am I to do this?”

segs.p: “Ehi tvaṁ, gāmaṇi, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ evaṁ vadehi:
segs.e: “Here, brahmin, go to the ascetic Gotama and say to him:

segs.p: ‘nanu, bhante, bhagavā anekapariyāyena kulānaṁ anuddayaṁ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṁ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṁ vaṇṇetī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Sir, don’t you in many ways praise kindness, protection, and sympathy for families?’

segs.p: Sace kho, gāmaṇi, samaṇo gotamo evaṁ puṭṭho evaṁ byākaroti:
segs.e: When he’s asked this, if he answers:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato anekapariyāyena kulānaṁ anuddayaṁ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṁ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṁ vaṇṇetī’ti, tamenaṁ tvaṁ evaṁ vadeyyāsi:
segs.e: ‘Indeed I do, chief,’ say this to him:

segs.p: ‘atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā dubbhikkhe dvīhitike setaṭṭhike salākāvutte mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ cārikaṁ carati?
segs.e: ‘So what then are you doing, wandering together with this large Saṅgha of mendicants during a time of famine and scarcity, with crops blighted and turned to straw?

segs.p: Ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno’ti.
segs.e: The Buddha is practicing to annihilate, collapse, and ruin families!’

segs.p: Imaṁ kho te, gāmaṇi, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṁ pañhaṁ puṭṭho neva sakkhati uggilituṁ, neva sakkhati ogilitun”ti.
segs.e: When you put this dilemma to him, the Buddha won’t be able to either spit it out or swallow it down.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā nigaṇṭhaṁ nāṭaputtaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Asibandhaka’s son. He rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Jain Ñātika, keeping him on his right. Then he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Nanu, bhante, bhagavā anekapariyāyena kulānaṁ anuddayaṁ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṁ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṁ vaṇṇetī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, don’t you in many ways praise kindness, protection, and sympathy for families?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato anekapariyāyena kulānaṁ anuddayaṁ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṁ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṁ vaṇṇetī”ti.
segs.e: “Indeed I do, chief.”

segs.p: “Atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā dubbhikkhe dvīhitike setaṭṭhike salākāvutte mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ cārikaṁ carati?
segs.e: “So what then are you doing, wandering together with this large Saṅgha of mendicants during a time of famine and scarcity, with crops blighted and turned to straw?

segs.p: Ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno”ti.
segs.e: The Buddha is practicing to annihilate, collapse, and ruin families!”

segs.p: “Ito so, gāmaṇi, ekanavutikappe yamahaṁ anussarāmi, nābhijānāmi kiñci kulaṁ pakkabhikkhānuppadānamattena upahatapubbaṁ.
segs.e: “Well, chief, I recollect ninety-one eons back but I’m not aware of any family that’s been ruined merely by offering some cooked almsfood.

segs.p: Atha kho yāni tāni kulāni aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni, sabbāni tāni dānasambhūtāni ceva saccasambhūtāni ca sāmaññasambhūtāni ca.
segs.e: Rather, rich, affluent, and wealthy families—with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain—all acquired their wealth because of giving, truth, and restraint.

segs.p: Aṭṭha kho, gāmaṇi, hetū, aṭṭha paccayā kulānaṁ upaghātāya.
segs.e: Chief, there are eight causes and reasons for the ruin of families.

segs.p: Rājato vā kulāni upaghātaṁ gacchanti, corato vā kulāni upaghātaṁ gacchanti, aggito vā kulāni upaghātaṁ gacchanti, udakato vā kulāni upaghātaṁ gacchanti, nihitaṁ vā ṭhānā vigacchati, duppayuttā vā kammantā vipajjanti, kule vā kulaṅgāroti uppajjati, yo te bhoge vikirati vidhamati viddhaṁseti, aniccatāyeva aṭṭhamīti.
segs.e: Their ruin stems from rulers, bandits, fire, or flood. Or they lose their savings. Or their business fails due to not applying themselves to work. Or a wastrel is born into the family who squanders and fritters away their wealth. And impermanence is the eighth.

segs.p: Ime kho, gāmaṇi, aṭṭha hetū, aṭṭha paccayā kulānaṁ upaghātāya.
segs.e: These are the eight causes and reasons for the ruin of families.

segs.p: Imesu kho, gāmaṇi, aṭṭhasu hetūsu, aṭṭhasu paccayesu saṁvijjamānesu yo maṁ evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Given that these eight reasons are found, suppose someone says this:

segs.p: ‘ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṁ paṭipanno’ti,
segs.e: ‘The Buddha is practicing to annihilate, collapse, and ruin families!’

segs.p: taṁ, gāmaṇi, vācaṁ appahāya taṁ cittaṁ appahāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye”ti.
segs.e: Unless they give up that speech and that thought, and let go of that view, they will be placed in hell as if delivered there.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Asibandhaka’s son the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.

segs.e: 1. Chiefs

segs.p: Maṇicūḷakasutta
segs.e: With Maṇicūḷaka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena rājantepure rājaparisāya sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time while the king’s retinue was sitting together in the royal compound this discussion came up among them,

segs.p: “kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ jātarūparajataṁ, sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajatan”ti.
segs.e: “Gold and currency are proper for ascetics who follow the Sakyan. They accept and receive gold and currency.”

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi tassaṁ parisāyaṁ nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time the chief Maṇicūḷaka was sitting in that assembly.

segs.p: Atha kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi taṁ parisaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He said to that retinue,

segs.p: “mā ayyo evaṁ avacuttha.
segs.e: “Good masters, don’t say that.

segs.p: Na kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ jātarūparajataṁ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā”ti.
segs.e: Gold and currency are not proper for ascetics who follow the Sakyan. They neither accept nor receive gold and currency. They have set aside gems and gold, and quit using gold and currency.”

segs.p: Asakkhi kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi taṁ parisaṁ saññāpetuṁ.
segs.e: He was able to persuade that assembly.

segs.p: Atha kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Maṇicūḷaka went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. He then said,

segs.p: “idha, bhante, rājantepure rājaparisāya sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
‘kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ jātarūparajataṁ, sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajatan’ti.
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ, bhante, taṁ parisaṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘mā ayyo evaṁ avacuttha.

Na kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ jātarūparajataṁ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā’ti.
Asakkhiṁ khvāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ parisaṁ saññāpetuṁ.

Kaccāhaṁ, bhante, evaṁ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva bhagavato homi, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhāmi, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaromi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchatī”ti?
segs.e: “Answering this way, I trust that I repeat what the Buddha has said, and don’t misrepresent him with an untruth. I trust my explanation is in line with the teaching, and that there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

segs.p: “Taggha tvaṁ, gāmaṇi, evaṁ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me hosi, na ca maṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhasi, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākarosi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati.
segs.e: “Indeed, in answering this way you repeat what I’ve said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Your explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.

segs.p: Na hi, gāmaṇi, kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ jātarūparajataṁ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṁ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā.
segs.e: Gold and currency are not proper for ascetics who follow the Sakyan. They neither accept nor receive gold and currency. They have set aside gems and gold, and quit using gold and currency.

segs.p: Yassa kho, gāmaṇi, jātarūparajataṁ kappati, pañcapi tassa kāmaguṇā kappanti.
segs.e: If gold and currency were proper for them, then the five kinds of sensual stimulation would also be proper.

segs.p: Yassa pañca kāmaguṇā kappanti (…), ekaṁsenetaṁ, gāmaṇi, dhāreyyāsi assamaṇadhammo asakyaputtiyadhammoti.
segs.e: And if the five kinds of sensual stimulation are proper for them, you should categorically regard them as not having the qualities of an ascetic or a follower of the Sakyan.

segs.p: Api cāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, evaṁ vadāmi—
segs.e: Rather, chief, I say this:

segs.p: tiṇaṁ tiṇatthikena pariyesitabbaṁ, dāru dārutthikena pariyesitabbaṁ, sakaṭaṁ sakaṭatthikena pariyesitabbaṁ, puriso purisatthikena pariyesitabbo.
segs.e: Straw may be looked for by one needing straw; wood may be looked for by one needing wood; a cart may be looked for by one needing a cart; a workman may be looked for by one needing a workman.

segs.p: Na tvevāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, kenaci pariyāyena ‘jātarūparajataṁ sāditabbaṁ pariyesitabban’ti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: But in any case, there is no way they can accept or look for gold and currency, I say.”

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.

segs.p: Bhadrakasutta
segs.e: With Bhadraka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu viharati uruvelakappaṁ nāma mallānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Mallas, near the Mallian town named Uruvelakappa.

segs.p: Atha kho bhadrako gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Bhadraka the village chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desetū”ti.
segs.e: “Please, sir, let the Blessed One teach me the origin and disappearance of suffering.”

segs.p: “Ahañce te, gāmaṇi, atītamaddhānaṁ ārabbha dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṁ:
segs.e: “Chief, if I were to teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering in connection with the past, saying

segs.p: ‘evaṁ ahosi atītamaddhānan’ti, tatra te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati.
segs.e: ‘this is how it was in the past,’ you might have doubts or uncertainties about that.

segs.p: Ahañce te, gāmaṇi, anāgatamaddhānaṁ ārabbha dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṁ:
segs.e: If I were to teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering in connection with the future, saying

segs.p: ‘evaṁ bhavissati anāgatamaddhānan’ti, tatrāpi te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati.
segs.e: ‘this is how it will be in the future,’ you might have doubts or uncertainties about that.

segs.p: Api cāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, idheva nisinno ettheva te nisinnassa dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmi.
segs.e: Rather, chief, I will teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering as I am sitting right here and you are sitting right there.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Bhadraka replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: “What do you think, chief?

segs.p: atthi te uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
segs.e: Are there any people here in Uruvelakappa who, if they were executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, it would cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

segs.p: “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
segs.e: “There are, sir.”

segs.p: “Atthi pana te, gāmaṇi, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
segs.e: “But are there any people here in Uruvelakappa who, if they were executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, it would not cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

segs.p: “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
segs.e: “There are, sir.”

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ko paccayo yena te ekaccānaṁ uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
segs.e: “What’s the cause, chief, what’s the reason why, if this was to happen to some people it could cause you sorrow, while if it happens to others it does not?”

segs.p: “Yesaṁ me, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, atthi me tesu chandarāgo.
segs.e: “The people regarding whom this would give rise to sorrow are those I have desire and passion.

segs.p: Yesaṁ pana, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, natthi me tesu chandarāgo”ti.
segs.e: The people regarding whom this would not give rise to sorrow are those I don’t have desire and passion.”

segs.p: “Iminā tvaṁ, gāmaṇi, dhammena diṭṭhena viditena akālikena pattena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgate nayaṁ nehi:
segs.e: “With this present phenomenon that you have seen, understood, immediately attained, and fathomed, you can apply the same method to the past and future:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kho kiñci atītamaddhānaṁ dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajji sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
segs.e: ‘All the suffering that arose in the past was rooted and sourced in desire.

segs.p: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassa.
segs.e: For desire is the root of suffering.

segs.p: Yampi hi kiñci anāgatamaddhānaṁ dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjissati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
segs.e: All the suffering that will arise in the future will be rooted and sourced in desire.

segs.p: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’”ti.
segs.e: For desire is the root of suffering.’”

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Yāva subhāsitañcidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā:
segs.e: How well said this was by the Buddha!

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
segs.e: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

segs.p: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’ti.
segs.e: For desire is the root of suffering.’

segs.p: Atthi me, bhante, ciravāsī nāma kumāro bahi āvasathe paṭivasati.
segs.e: I have a boy called Ciravāsi, who resides in a house away from here.

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, kālasseva vuṭṭhāya purisaṁ uyyojemi:
segs.e: I rise early and dispatch someone, saying:

segs.p: ‘gaccha, bhaṇe, ciravāsiṁ kumāraṁ jānāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, lad, and check on my boy Ciravāsi.’

segs.p: Yāvakīvañca, bhante, so puriso nāgacchati, tassa me hoteva aññathattaṁ:
segs.e: Until they get back I worry:

segs.p: ‘mā heva ciravāsissa kumārassa kiñci ābādhayitthā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I hope nothing’s wrong with Ciravāsi!’”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: “What do you think, chief?

segs.p: ciravāsissa kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
segs.e: If Ciravāsi was executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, would it cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

segs.p: “Ciravāsissa me, bhante, kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṁ, kiṁ pana me nuppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
segs.e: “How could it not, sir?”

segs.p: “Imināpi kho etaṁ, gāmaṇi, pariyāyena veditabbaṁ:
segs.e: “This too is a way to understand:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
segs.e: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

segs.p: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’ti.
segs.e: For desire is the root of suffering.’

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: What do you think, chief?

segs.p: yadā te ciravāsimātā adiṭṭhā ahosi, assutā ahosi, te ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
segs.e: Before you’d seen or heard of Ciravāsi’s mother, did you have any desire or passion or fondness for her?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Dassanaṁ vā te, gāmaṇi, āgamma savanaṁ vā evaṁ te ahosi:
segs.e: “Then was it because you saw or heard of her that you had

segs.p: ‘ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: desire or passion or fondness for her?”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
segs.e: “What do you think, chief?

segs.p: ciravāsimātuyā te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?

segs.e: “This too is a way to understand:

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
segs.e: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

segs.e: 1. Chiefs

segs.p: Rāsiyasutta
segs.e: With Rāsiya

segs.p: Atha kho rāsiyo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rāsiyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Rāsiya the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante, ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṁ tapaṁ garahati, sabbaṁ tapassiṁ lūkhajīviṁ ekaṁsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I have heard this: ‘The ascetic Gotama criticizes all forms of mortification. He categorically condemns and denounces those fervent mortifiers who live rough.’

segs.p: Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṁsu: ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṁ tapaṁ garahati, sabbaṁ tapassiṁ lūkhajīviṁ ekaṁsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchatī”ti?
segs.e: I trust those who say this repeat what the Buddha has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

segs.p: “Ye te, gāmaṇi, evamāhaṁsu: ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṁ tapaṁ garahati, sabbaṁ tapassiṁ lūkhajīviṁ ekaṁsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti, na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṁ te asatā tucchā abhūtena.
segs.e: “Chief, those who say this do not repeat what I have said. They misrepresent me with what is false, hollow, and untrue.

segs.p: Dveme, gāmaṇi, antā pabbajitena na sevitabbā—
segs.e: These two extremes should not be cultivated by one gone forth.

segs.p: yo cāyaṁ kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogo hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṁhito, yo cāyaṁ attakilamathānuyogo dukkho anariyo anatthasaṁhito.
segs.e: Indulgence in sensual pleasures, which is low, crude, ordinary, ignoble, and pointless. And indulgence in self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and pointless.

segs.p: Ete te, gāmaṇi, ubho ante anupagamma majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā—cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One understood the middle way of practice, which gives vision and knowledge, and leads to peace, direct knowledge, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Katamā ca sā, gāmaṇi, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā—cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati?
segs.e: And what is that middle way of practice?

segs.p: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, gāmaṇi, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā—cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This, chief, is the middle way of practice that was understood by the Realized One, which gives vision and knowledge, and leads to peace, direct knowledge, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Tayo kho me, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogino santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: There are these three pleasure seekers in the world.

segs.p: Katame tayo?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati, sāhasena adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: Take a pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means, and who doesn’t make themselves happy and pleased, or share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena.
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means.

segs.p: Adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, but don’t share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena.
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means.

segs.p: Adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, and they share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi.
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive.

segs.p: Dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na attānaṁ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati, na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They don’t make themselves happy and pleased, or share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi.
segs.e: Next, a pleasure seeker seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive.

segs.p: Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati, na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They don’t make themselves happy and pleased, or share it and make merit.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena.

segs.p: Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased, and they share it and make merit.

segs.p: Te ca bhoge gadhito mucchito ajjhopanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: They enjoy that wealth tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

segs.p: Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena.

segs.e: And they enjoy that wealth untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape.

segs.p: Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṁ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati, na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using illegitimate, coercive means, and who doesn’t make themselves happy and pleased, or share it and make merit.

segs.e: They may be criticized on three grounds.

segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: They seek wealth using illegitimate, coercive means. This is the first ground for criticism.

segs.p: Na attānaṁ sukheti na pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: They don’t make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for criticism.

segs.p: Na saṁvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho.

segs.p: Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti saṁvibhajati puññāni karoti.
segs.e: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using means both legitimate and illegitimate, and coercive and non-coercive, and who makes themselves happy and pleased, and shares it and makes merit.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso, ekena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: They may be praised on three grounds, and criticized on one.

segs.p: Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso?
segs.e: What are the three grounds for praise?

segs.p: Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They seek wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means. This is the first ground for praise.

segs.p: Attānaṁ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They make themselves happy and pleased. This is the second ground for praise.

segs.p: Saṁvibhajati puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṁso.
segs.e: They share it and make merit. This is the third ground for praise.

segs.p: Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho?
segs.e: What is the one ground for criticism?

segs.p: Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: They seek wealth using illegitimate, coercive means. This is the one ground for criticism.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṁso, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.
segs.e: This pleasure seeker may be praised on these three grounds, and criticized on this one.

segs.p: Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṁ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena, na attānaṁ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṁvibhajati, na puññāni karoti.
segs.e: Now, consider the pleasure seeker who seeks wealth using legitimate, non-coercive means, but who doesn’t make themselves happy and pleased, or share it and make merit.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena pāsaṁso, dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

segs.e: They don’t share it and make merit. This is the second ground for criticism.

segs.p: Tayome, gāmaṇi, tapassino lūkhajīvino santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These three fervent mortifiers who live rough are found in the world.

segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco tapassī lūkhajīvī saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
segs.e: Take a fervent mortifier who has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

segs.p: Tisso imā, gāmaṇi, sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: There are these three kinds of wearing away that are apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know them for themselves.

segs.p: Katamā tisso?
segs.e: What three?

segs.p: Yaṁ ratto rāgādhikaraṇaṁ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti.
segs.e: A greedy person, because of greed, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

segs.p: Rāge pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti.
segs.e: When they’ve given up greed they don’t have such intentions.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Yaṁ duṭṭho dosādhikaraṇaṁ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti.
segs.e: A hateful person, because of hate, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

segs.p: Dose pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti.
segs.e: When they’ve given up hate they don’t have such intentions.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Yaṁ mūḷho mohādhikaraṇaṁ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti.
segs.e: A deluded person, because of delusion, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both.

segs.p: Mohe pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti.
segs.e: When they’ve given up delusion they don’t have such intentions.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Imā kho, gāmaṇi, tisso sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhī”ti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of wearing away that are apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know them for themselves.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, rāsiyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Rāsiya the chief said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe…
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! Excellent! …

segs.p: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
