segs.p: Pāṭaliyasutta
segs.e: With Pāṭaliya

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā koliyesu viharati uttaraṁ nāma koliyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Koliyans, where they have a town named Uttarakā.

segs.p: Atha kho pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Pāṭaliya the chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “sutaṁ metaṁ, bhante:
segs.e: “Sir, I have heard this:

segs.p: ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṁ jānātī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The ascetic Gotama knows deceit.’

segs.p: Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṁsu: ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṁ jānātī’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati?
segs.e: I trust those who say this repeat what the Buddha has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?

segs.p: Anabbhācikkhitukāmā hi mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavantan”ti.
segs.e: For we don’t want to misrepresent the Blessed One.”

segs.p: “Ye te, gāmaṇi, evamāhaṁsu: ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṁ jānātī’ti, vuttavādino ceva me, te na ca maṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchatī”ti.
segs.e: “Chief, those who say this repeat what I have said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Their explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.”

segs.p: “Saccaṁyeva kira, bho, mayaṁ tesaṁ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ na saddahāma:
segs.e: “Sir, we didn’t believe that what those ascetics and brahmins said was really true.

segs.p: ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṁ jānātī’ti, samaṇo khalu bho gotamo māyāvī”ti.
segs.e: But it seems the ascetic Gotama is deceitful!”

segs.p: “Tatra, gāmaṇi, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṁvādino evaṁdiṭṭhino:
segs.e: “Since this is so, the ascetics and brahmins whose view is that

segs.p: ‘yo koci musā bhaṇati, sabbo so diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti, saccaṁ vā te āhaṁsu musā vā”ti?
segs.e: everyone who lies experiences pain and sadness in this very life: are they right or wrong?”

segs.p: “Musā, bhante”.
segs.e: “They’re wrong, sir.”

segs.p: “Ye pana te tucchaṁ musā vilapanti sīlavanto vā te dussīlā vā”ti?
segs.e: “But those who speak hollow, false nonsense: are they moral or immoral?”

segs.p: “Dussīlā, bhante”.
segs.e: “Immoral, sir.”

segs.p: “Ye pana te dussīlā pāpadhammā micchāpaṭipannā vā te sammāpaṭipannā vā”ti?
segs.e: “And are those who are immoral, of bad character practicing wrongly or rightly?”

segs.p: “Micchāpaṭipannā, bhante”.
segs.e: “They’re practicing wrongly, sir.”

segs.p: “Ye pana te micchāpaṭipannā micchādiṭṭhikā vā te sammādiṭṭhikā vā”ti?
segs.e: “And do those who are practicing wrongly have wrong view or right view?”

segs.p: “Micchādiṭṭhikā, bhante”.
segs.e: “They have wrong view, sir.”

segs.p: “Ye pana te micchādiṭṭhikā kallaṁ nu tesu pasīditun”ti?
segs.e: “But is it appropriate to have confidence in those of wrong view?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.

segs.p: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
segs.e: It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Atthi me, bhante, āvasathāgāraṁ.
segs.e: I have a guest house,

segs.p: Tattha atthi mañcakāni, atthi āsanāni, atthi udakamaṇiko, atthi telappadīpo.
segs.e: where there are cots, seats, water jars, and oil lamps.

segs.p: Tattha yo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā vāsaṁ upeti, tenāhaṁ yathāsatti yathābalaṁ saṁvibhajāmi.
segs.e: Whenever an ascetic or brahmin comes to stay, I share what I have as best I can.

segs.p: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhante, cattāro satthāro nānādiṭṭhikā nānākhantikā nānārucikā, tasmiṁ āvasathāgāre vāsaṁ upagacchuṁ.
segs.e: Once it so happened, sir, that four teachers of different views, beliefs, and opinions came to stay at my guest house.

segs.p: Eko satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko. Natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

segs.p: Eko satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘atthi dinnaṁ, atthi yiṭṭhaṁ, atthi hutaṁ, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, atthi ayaṁ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā, ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.

segs.p: Eko satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: One teacher had this doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato, adinnaṁ ādiyato, sandhiṁ chindato, nillopaṁ harato, ekāgārikaṁ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṁ gacchato, musā bhaṇato, karoto na karīyati pāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘The one who acts does nothing wrong when they punish, mutilate, torture, aggrieve, oppress, intimidate, or when they encourage others to do the same. Nothing bad is done when they kill, steal, break into houses, plunder wealth, steal from isolated buildings, commit highway robbery, commit adultery, and lie.

segs.p: Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṁ maṁsakhalaṁ ekaṁ maṁsapuñjaṁ kareyya, natthi tatonidānaṁ pāpaṁ, natthi pāpassa āgamo.
segs.e: If you were to reduce all the living creatures of this earth to one heap and mass of flesh with a razor-edged chakram, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

segs.e: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, no evil comes of that, and no outcome of evil.

segs.p: Uttarañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṁ gaccheyya dadanto dāpento yajanto yajāpento, natthi tatonidānaṁ puññaṁ, natthi puññassa āgamo.
segs.e: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, no merit comes of that, and no outcome of merit.

segs.p: Dānena damena saṁyamena saccavajjena natthi puññaṁ, natthi puññassa āgamo’ti.
segs.e: In giving, self-control, restraint, and truthfulness there is no merit or outcome of merit.’

segs.e: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, ahudeva kaṅkhā, ahu vicikicchā:
segs.e: I had doubt and uncertainty about that:

segs.p: ‘kosu nāma imesaṁ bhavataṁ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ saccaṁ āha, ko musā’”ti?
segs.e: ‘I wonder who of these respected ascetics and brahmins speaks the truth, and who speaks falsehood?’”

segs.p: “Alañhi te, gāmaṇi, kaṅkhituṁ, alaṁ vicikicchituṁ.
segs.e: “Chief, no wonder you’re doubting and uncertain.

segs.p: Kaṅkhanīye ca pana te ṭhāne vicikicchā uppannā”ti.
segs.e: Doubt has come up in you about an uncertain matter.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ pasannohaṁ, bhante, bhagavati. Pahoti me bhagavā tathā dhammaṁ desetuṁ yathāhaṁ imaṁ kaṅkhādhammaṁ pajaheyyan”ti.
segs.e: “I am quite confident that the Buddha is capable of teaching me so that I can give up this state of uncertainty.”

segs.p: “Atthi, gāmaṇi, dhammasamādhi.
segs.e: “Chief, there is immersion based on understanding of principle.

segs.p: Tatra ce tvaṁ cittasamādhiṁ paṭilabheyyāsi. Evaṁ tvaṁ imaṁ kaṅkhādhammaṁ pajaheyyāsi.
segs.e: If you gain such mental immersion, you can give up that state of uncertainty.

segs.p: Katamo ca, gāmaṇi, dhammasamādhi?
segs.e: And what is immersion based on understanding of principle?

segs.p: Idha, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācāraṁ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusaṁ vācaṁ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpaṁ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, abhijjhaṁ pahāya anabhijjhālu hoti, byāpādapadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiṁ pahāya sammādiṭṭhiko hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has given up killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, backbiting, harsh speech, talking nonsense, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako evaṁ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ, tathā tatiyaṁ, tathā catutthaṁ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: Then that noble disciple is rid of desire, rid of ill will, unconfused, aware, and mindful. They meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.e: They reflect thus:

segs.p: ‘yvāyaṁ satthā evaṁvādī evaṁdiṭṭhi:
segs.e: ‘That teacher who had this doctrine and view:

segs.e: Being joyful, rapture springs up.

segs.e: When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.

segs.e: When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.

segs.p: Sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.
segs.e: And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, gāmaṇi, dhammasamādhi.
segs.e: This is that immersion based on understanding of principle.

segs.e: If you were to go along the south bank of the Ganges killing, mutilating, and torturing, and encouraging others to do the same, evil comes of that, and an outcome of evil.

segs.e: If you were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving and sacrificing and encouraging others to do the same, merit comes of that, and an outcome of merit.
